questions.q: What is the real difference between trigger(availableNow=True) and trigger(processingTime="30 seconds")?
options: processingTime runs indefinitely on a fixed interval; availableNow processes what's currently new, once, then stops
They are functionally identical in every case
availableNow requires file notification mode; processingTime does not
processingTime only works with batch DataFrames, never streaming ones
questions.explain: processingTime is what makes a pipeline genuinely continuous instead of a one-shot scheduled catch-up job.

questions.q: What does foreachBatch let a single Auto Loader stream do that a plain toTable sink cannot?
options: Run ordinary batch-DataFrame code per micro-batch, including writing to more than one table
Skip schema inference entirely
Automatically switch from directory listing to file notification mode
Process files without ever creating a checkpoint
questions.explain: foreachBatch hands each micro-batch to custom batch logic, enabling multiple sinks or other custom processing per batch.

questions.q: How can you check whether a continuously running stream is healthy without stopping it?
options: query.status and query.lastProgress
Re-reading the entire source directory manually
Dropping and recreating the checkpoint location
There is no way to check a running stream's health
questions.explain: These properties on the streaming query object report live health and recent progress without interrupting the stream.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does the Kafka course's Lesson 26 use the same Structured Streaming API for?
options: Reading a live Kafka topic with readStream.format("kafka"), using the same triggers and foreachBatch pattern
Running Auto Loader against a Kafka-backed file system
Replacing Unity Catalog entirely with Kafka's own governance model
A completely unrelated streaming engine with no shared API
questions.explain: Kafka and Auto Loader are both just sources plugged into the same underlying Structured Streaming engine and API.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what did Databricks & Delta Lake Lessons 32-33 already establish?
options: The basic cloudFiles-to-writeStream combination with trigger(availableNow=True), running once until caught up
foreachBatch writing to multiple sinks from one stream
query.status and query.lastProgress for monitoring a continuous stream
Reading a live Kafka topic with Structured Streaming
questions.explain: This lesson recaps that one-shot combination before covering continuous triggers, multi-sink batches, and live monitoring.
